reason: The Hebrew text depicts the Israelites complaining about their bondage and hard slavery in Egypt, not about their leaders. Specifically, the passage shows they sigh/groan (וַיֵּאָנְח) and cry out (וַיִּזְעָ֑קוּ) because of their servitude (מִן־ הָעֲבֹדָה), with their complaints directed to God about their affliction. When Moses delivers God's message to the Israelites, they actually refuse to listen to him (וְלֹא שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה) due to despair and hard labor, but this is not portrayed as complaining about their leadership—rather, it shows their inability to receive hope amid distress.
